fourteen years. And when he went to Thrace in the war with the Bulgars, there too he drank and caroused; therefore the leaders agreed with his mother,
and when he returned, she put antimony into his eyes, and he was blinded;
and she reigned alone.
And she made her second-in-command and the head of the patricians Aetios the eunuch.
And when the Arabs invaded the territory of the Romans,
Aetios defeated them.
And after a year, when the Arabs invaded, Aetios was defeated.
And again the Arabs invaded and were victorious.
Then the Romans desired to make Nikephoros Logothete the Cappadocian king.
And when Irene heard, she commanded that they should put antimony into his eyes;
and Aetios the eunuch hid him.
Then Niketas the patrician and patriarch took counsel with the senate,
and it seemed good to all of them that Nikephoros should reign.
And he began to reign in the year 1114
(1114 of the Greeks,
803 of our Lord).
And he held Queen Irene and Aetios the eunuch in honor;
they, however, prepared his murder by means of certain monks.
And when the plot was revealed,
Irene was sent into exile to Athens,
and there she became a nun.
And to Aetios he repaid the kindness {OCR?} according to what he had done for him.
And the king did not harm {OCR?} the monks.
At this time, while Harun Rashid was occupied with the building of the city of Zibatra in Lesser Armenia near Melitene,
Staurakios, the commander of the army of the Romans, invaded the land of the Peloponnese, which had belonged to the Arabs for a long time,
and he subjugated it and placed a garrison in it,
and he returned, driving off a great multitude of captives of the Arab people,
and flocks of sheep {OCR?} and herds of horses and camels.
And it is said
that a certain Arab, Jabala, was king of the Christian Arabs.
And when, through Umar ibn al-Khattab, he became a Muslim and was present with him in the mosque in Yathrib,
a man from the tribe called Fazara stepped on him.
And he turned and struck him and broke his nose.
And when the Fazari complained,
Umar said to Jabala,
"Appease him,
or surrender your nose to him to be broken."
He, however, answered,
"How can a king like me
permit an inferior to strike him?" And Umar said,
"Even though you are more honored than he in royalty,
yet you are equal to him in Islam."
And Jabala said,
"Leave me until morning,
that I may consider one of the two things that you have told me."
